mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -42.1% to -37.6%, a 4.5 percentage point gain over two weeks) signals momentum recovery in discretionary mobility. This positive trend will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the baseline mean of the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -37.6% or declines further, indicating the recovery trend reversed.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved steadily (from -34.9% to -29.6%, a 5.3 point gain), indicating commuters are returning to public transport. This restoration of commuting infrastructure access will enable retail visits bundled with transit-dependent trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -34.9% to -29.6% over two weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility reverses (declines more than 2 points week-on-week) while RETAIL_REC remains below -35%, breaking the assumed causal link.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has improved consistently (from -14.7% to -9.9%, a 4.8 point gain), indicating essential-trip frequency is rising. Consumers making more frequent essential trips will increase incidental retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 percentage points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 4.8 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stalls or declines while RETAIL_REC fails to improve, indicating no spillover effect from essential to discretionary mobility.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered (from -33.0% to -30.4%, a 2.6 point gain) while RESIDENTIAL confinement has eased (from 12.0% to 10.6%, a 1.4 point decline). This dual signal of workplace return and reduced home-staying will compound to drive retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves AND RESIDENTIAL declines simultaneously over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 2.6 points and RESIDENTIAL declined 1.4 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or RESIDENTIAL reverses direction while the other stalls, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both signals improving.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains severely depressed (at -59.1%), indicating outdoor recreation is still heavily restricted or avoided. If PARKS mobility fails to improve over the next week, consumers will substitute toward indoor retail venues, sustaining elevated RETAIL_REC relative to the current baseline.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -55% in the next week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -59.1% in t-0w, showing no recovery trajectory
failure_condition: PARKS mobility improves by more than 10 percentage points in the next week, indicating a shift to outdoor recreation that diverts retail traffic.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains significantly depressed (at -29.6%) while RETAIL_REC has improved to -37.6%. This divergence suggests retail recovery is driven by local/walking-distance visits rather than transit-dependent trips. If TRANSIT fails to recover faster than RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, the local-retail mechanism will dominate, sustaining RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by less than 3 percentage points while RETAIL_REC improves by more than 2 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -29.6% and RETAIL_REC at -37.6% show divergent recovery rates
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves faster than RETAIL_REC (by more than 2 points differential), suggesting transit-dependent retail is the binding constraint and RETAIL_REC will plateau.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL confinement has declined steadily (from 12.4% to 10.6% over three weeks), indicating a consistent weekly easing of stay-at-home behavior. This trend will continue over the next four weeks, progressively releasing suppressed retail demand and driving RETAIL_REC higher.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by more than 0.5 percentage points per week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.8 points from t-3w to t-0w at a steady rate
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL confinement stabilizes or increases while RETAIL_REC fails to improve, indicating the easing of home-staying is not translating to retail visits.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT have both improved consistently, signaling that essential-trip infrastructure and commuting are recovering in tandem. This dual recovery will enable bundled trips (transit to grocery to retail), creating a multiplicative effect that drives RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: Both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT improve by more than 2 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 4.8 points and TRANSIT improved 5.3 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM or TRANSIT reverses direction while the other continues improving, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both proxies improving.
